builder_plan.scenario: Your self-hosted model spends too long generating answers token by token.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a compatible draft model and serving integration exist before renting compute.
builder_plan.baseline: The same target with speculation off, then your existing drafter if you have one.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted draft length, tokens per second, tail latency, output quality, and total GPU cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Cord: Confidence-Anchored Order Residual Decoding for Masked Diffusion Language Models
summary: Replaces uniform confidence-based reveal order in masked diffusion LLMs with a lightweight contextual-bandit policy that learns prompt-conditioned residual adjustments to generation direction, proximity, and two-sided infilling. Costs 0.53M additional parameters, a per-rollout coefficient matrix, and 5.39% inference latency overhead, with no extra backbone forward passes. Can fail if sequence-level rewards are noisy or misaligned, since there is no step-level credit assignment and the learned residual policy may not transfer across tasks, models, or decoding settings.
rationale: The method is small enough to trial without infrastructure expansion, but its value depends on whether masked-diffusion decoding and reward-defined task success match the reader's production workload.

claims.statement: Replaces uniform confidence-based reveal order in masked diffusion LLMs with a lightweight contextual-bandit policy that learns prompt-conditioned residual adjustments to generation direction, proximity, and two-sided infilling. Costs 0.53M additional parameters, a per-rollout coefficient matrix, and 5.39% inference latency overhead, with no extra backbone forward passes. Can fail if sequence-level rewards are noisy or misaligned, since there is no step-level credit assignment and the learned residual policy may not transfer across tasks, models, or decoding settings.
Improves average task success from 32.0% under confidence decoding to 48.2% across three dLLMs and five reasoning, code, and constraint-satisfaction benchmarks.
